questions.question: What feature was used on Golconda Fort's gates to protect it during attacks involving war elephants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Steel spikes on doors**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Steel spikes** were strategically installed on the gates of Golconda Fort to prevent war elephants from ramming and breaking the gates during attacks.
 
• The spikes were pointed and sharp, making it impossible for elephants to use their strength to push or damage the gates.
 
• This feature was a common defensive mechanism in medieval Indian forts to counter the use of war elephants by invading armies.
 
• The gates of Golconda Fort were also designed with robust wooden structures, reinforced with steel to withstand heavy impacts.
 
• The strategic use of these spikes showcases the advanced engineering and defensive architecture of the era, ensuring the fort's safety during sieges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deep moat with water channels:**

 
 
• Moats were commonly used as a defensive feature in forts to prevent enemy forces from approaching the fort walls easily.
 
• Filled with water, moats acted as a barrier against infantry and cavalry attacks.
 
• However, Golconda Fort did not primarily rely on moats for defense against war elephants; the steel spikes were the preferred solution.
 
 
 
• **Electrified spikes:**
 
 
• This option is incorrect as the technology for electrified spikes was not available during the time of Golconda Fort's construction.
 
• Electricity was discovered centuries after the fort was built, making this an anachronistic suggestion.
 
 
 
• **Stone cannon towers:**
 
 
• Stone cannon towers were used for defensive purposes to place cannons for firing at approaching enemies.
 
• While the fort did have cannon towers, they were not specifically used to defend against war elephants.
 
• Cannons were primarily aimed at infantry, siege equipment, and other large-scale attackers.

questions.question: Which of the following best captures the core rituals and symbolism of the Fagli (Kus/Kuns) festival in Pattan Valley?

options.text: Baraza, symbolizing Shikhara-Appa, is made with marigold and turmeric and placed at village shrines.
Punha involves symbolic ploughing indoors using willow sticks, reflecting farming hopes during snow.
Totu, made of wheat and honey, is offered on rooftops to priests, then fed to goats.
Kwari sweets are made by elder women for temple offerings, as men chant to crow spirits.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punha involves symbolic ploughing indoors using willow sticks, reflecting farming hopes during snow.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fagli festival, celebrated in the Pattan Valley of Himachal Pradesh, is a traditional winter event celebrated to mark the end of the harsh winter season.
 
• **Punha**, one of the rituals, involves symbolic indoor ploughing using willow sticks, symbolizing hope and prosperity for agriculture in the upcoming season.
 
• This symbolic ritual is significant as it reflects the dependence of the local community on farming and their connection with nature, even during snow-covered winters.
 
• The festival emphasizes agricultural prosperity, community bonding, and the preparation for the upcoming farming season.
 
• The use of willow sticks indoors signifies adaptability and reverence toward nature, as agricultural activities halt during heavy snow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Some of the key festivals and fairs of Himachal Pradesh:**

 
 
• Kullu Dussehra (Kullu): A huge, unique Dussehra celebrated with traditional deities brought from villages, unlike other parts of India.
 
• Mandi Shivratri (Mandi): Features processions of local deities (Devtas) to the main temple, showcasing rich culture.
 
• Lavi Fair (Rampur Bushahr): An ancient trade fair, famous for trading wool, pashmina, and dry fruits, with significant cultural events.
 
• Shimla Summer Festival (Shimla): A multi-day cultural extravaganza held in summer, boosting tourism.
 
• Nalwari Fair (Bilaspur): A prominent cattle fair with wrestling and other activities.

questions.question: Determine the correctly matched Gupta fiscal term with its meaning.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vaishthika - forced or corvée labour**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Gupta administrative and fiscal system**, **Vaishthika** referred to **forced labour or corvée labour** imposed by the state. ***Hence, option 4 is correctly matched.***
 
• **Corvée labour** means compulsory unpaid labour provided by subjects for public works or state purposes.
 
• **Hiranya** referred to taxes paid in the form of **cash or precious metals**, not compulsory labour. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Dhanya** referred to taxes paid in the form of **grain or agricultural produce**, not gold tax. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Bhoga** denoted the **periodic supply of fruits, flowers, fuel, and other provisions** to the king or officials, rather than the king’s share of produce. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement-wise Analysis:**
 
 
• **Hiranya - compulsory labour service** – Incorrect.
 
• **Dhanya - gold tax** – Incorrect.
 
• **Bhoga - king's share of produce** – Incorrect.
 
• **Vaishthika - forced or corvée labour** – Correct.
 
 
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Vaishthika - forced or corvée labour.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gupta Empire:** The Gupta period lasted approximately from **320 CE to 550 CE** and is often called the **“Golden Age of Ancient India”**.
 
• **Main Sources:** Information about Gupta administration comes from **inscriptions, coins, land grants, and accounts of Chinese traveler Faxian**.
 
• **Land Revenue:** The major source of state income during the Gupta period was **land tax**, generally collected as a share of agricultural produce.
 
• **Bhaga:** The term **Bhaga** referred to the king’s share of produce, usually around **one-sixth** of the agricultural yield.
 
• **Economic System:** Both **cash payments** and **payments in kind** were common during the Gupta age.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Important Gupta Fiscal Terms:**

 
 
• **Hiranya** – Cash tax
 
• **Dhanya** – Tax in grain
 
• **Bhaga** – King’s share of produce
 
• **Vaishthika** – Forced labour
 
• **Bhoga** – Supplies or provisions to officials
 
 
 
• Questions related to **Gupta administration, taxation, and economic terms** are frequently asked in history and competitive examinations.

questions.question: Which musical instrument from Sikkim is believed to have been the first created for the deity Tetlara Lahadongna, and is associated with mythological origins?

• It is believed to have been crafted for the deity **Tetlara Lahadongna**, highlighting its mythological and spiritual significance.
 
• This instrument is made from natural materials, primarily bamboo, which reflects the eco-friendly practices and resourcefulness of the local communities.
 
• Simikla Koom (Binayo) is classified as a **wind instrument**, which produces sound through the vibration of air columns.
 
• The use of this instrument is deeply embedded in Sikkimese culture, often played during festivals, rituals, and traditional ceremonies.

• This is not a recognized traditional instrument from Sikkim, but the name may reflect a fictional or lesser-known term.

questions.question:
Match each ruler listed in Column A with their respective period of reign given in Column B:

 
 

 Column A: Ruler
 Column B: Reign Period
 
 

 A. Qutbuddin Aybak
 1. 1175-1192
 
 

 B. Prithviraj Chauhan
 2. 1206-1210
 
 

 C. Alauddin Khalji
 3. 1296-1316
 
 

 D. Muhammad Tughluq
 4. 1324-1351
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3: A → 2, B → 1, C → 3, D → 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Qutbuddin Aybak (1206–1210):** Qutbuddin Aybak was the founder of the Delhi Sultanate and the first ruler of the Slave Dynasty. He ruled from 1206 to 1210 and was known for constructing the Qutub Minar in Delhi.
 
• **Prithviraj Chauhan (1175–1192):** Prithviraj Chauhan was a Rajput king of the Chahamana dynasty who ruled during 1175–1192 CE. He is remembered for his valiant battles against Muhammad Ghori.
 
• **Alauddin Khalji (1296–1316):** Alauddin Khalji was the second ruler of the Khalji dynasty in India. His reign, from 1296 to 1316, is marked by military expansion and administrative reforms.
 
• **Muhammad bin Tughluq (1324–1351):** Muhammad bin Tughluq, the Sultan of Delhi, ruled from 1324 to 1351. He was known for his ambitious and often controversial reforms, such as the attempted introduction of token currency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Slave Dynasty (1206–1290):** The Slave Dynasty, also known as the Mamluk Dynasty, was the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. It was established by Qutbuddin Aybak, who was originally a slave of Muhammad Ghori. The dynasty laid the foundation of Muslim rule in India.
 
• **Chahamana Dynasty:** The Chahamanas (Chauhans) were a prominent Rajput dynasty that ruled over parts of northwestern India, including Delhi and Ajmer. Prithviraj Chauhan is the most celebrated ruler of this dynasty.
 
• **Khalji Dynasty (1290–1320):** This dynasty is known for its expansionist policies and economic reforms. Alauddin Khalji implemented price control measures and established a strong central administration.
 
• **Tughluq Dynasty (1320–1414):** The Tughluq dynasty was known for its ambitious rulers like Muhammad bin Tughluq, who attempted various reforms, including shifting the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad and the introduction of token currency. These reforms, however, were largely unsuccessful and led to administrative challenges.

questions.question:
**Fill in the blanks: **

At the 1984 Summer Olympics, P. T. Usha narrowly missed a bronze medal by ____ of a second.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One-hundredth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• P. T. Usha, popularly known as the "Payyoli Express," is one of India’s greatest athletes and a legend in track and field.
 
• At the 1984 Summer Olympics held in Los Angeles, she competed in the women’s 400m hurdles event.
 
• She narrowly missed the bronze medal, finishing fourth in the final with a timing of 55.42 seconds.
 
• The difference between P. T. Usha and the bronze medalist was just **one-hundredth (0.01) of a second**, making it a historic and heartbreaking moment in Indian sports history.
 
• Despite not winning a medal, her achievement remains significant as she became the first Indian woman to reach the finals of an Olympic event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1984 Summer Olympics:**

 
 
• The 1984 Summer Olympics were held in Los Angeles, USA, from July 28 to August 12.
 
• India’s participation in athletics was highlighted by P. T. Usha’s remarkable performance in the 400m hurdles.
 
• Her near-podium finish brought attention to Indian athletics on the global stage and inspired future generations of athletes.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Indica: A Deep Natural History of the Indian Subcontinent'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pranay Lal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pranay Lal** is the author of the critically acclaimed book '**Indica: A Deep Natural History of the Indian Subcontinent**'.
 
• The book presents an in-depth exploration of the geological, biological, and ecological history of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• 'Indica' is the first comprehensive account of the natural history of India, covering over 4.5 billion years of Earth's evolution.
 
• The book combines storytelling, scientific research, and illustrations to make complex topics accessible to a broad audience.
 
• It has been praised for its interdisciplinary approach, blending geology, paleontology, and biodiversity to paint a vivid picture of India's natural history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sanjeev Sanyal**

 
 
• Sanjeev Sanyal is an Indian economist and author known for works like *'The Ocean of Churn'* and *'The Indian Renaissance'*.
 
• His books primarily focus on history, economics, and the cultural heritage of India.
 
 
 
• **Rohan Murty**
 
 
• Rohan Murty is a computer scientist, entrepreneur, and founder of the **Murty Classical Library of India**.
 
• The Murty Classical Library of India publishes English translations of classical Indian texts to promote India's literary heritage.
 
 
 
• **Tony Joseph**
 
 
• Tony Joseph is the author of the popular book *'Early Indians: The Story of Our Ancestors and Where We Came From'*.
 
• The book delves into the genetic and archaeological history of the Indian subcontinent, focusing on human migration and settlement patterns.

questions.question: Uttar Pradesh accounted for approximately what percent of India's total population in 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the 2011 Census of India, Uttar Pradesh accounted for approximately **16%** (or 0.16) of the total population of India.
 
• The total population of India in 2011 was around 1.21 billion, and Uttar Pradesh contributed approximately **199.81 million** to this figure.
 
• Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state in India, followed by Maharashtra and Bihar.
 
• The state’s high population is attributed to factors such as a high fertility rate, large geographical area, and significant rural population.
 
• Uttar Pradesh alone has a population larger than many countries, ranking as the fifth most populous administrative unit globally, after China, India, the United States, and Indonesia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Dynamics of India **

 
 
• The Census of India, conducted every 10 years, is the most reliable source of demographic data for the country.
 
• India has a highly uneven distribution of population, with Uttar Pradesh being the most populous state, while states like Sikkim and Mizoram have much smaller populations.
 
• Population distribution in India is influenced by factors like fertility rates, migration, urbanization, and socioeconomic conditions.

questions.question: What does the designation HLVM3 stand for in the Gaganyaan mission context?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Human LVM3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The designation **HLVM3** stands for **Human LVM3**, which refers to the modified version of the Launch Vehicle Mark-3 (LVM3) developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) for the Gaganyaan mission.
 
• **LVM3**, also known as GSLV Mk-III, is India’s heaviest and most advanced rocket, capable of launching payloads up to 8 tons into low Earth orbit.
 
• For the Gaganyaan mission, LVM3 has been customized to carry humans safely into space, integrating advanced safety features such as an abort system and life-support mechanisms.
 
• The HLVM3 is equipped with a crew module and service module designed to house astronauts and ensure their safety during the mission.
 
• The Gaganyaan program aims to send a crew of three astronauts into low Earth orbit for a duration of up to seven days using the HLVM3 rocket.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gaganyaan Mission:**

 
 
• The Gaganyaan mission is India’s first human spaceflight program, aimed at demonstrating the capability of sending astronauts into space and bringing them back safely.
 
• It involves critical technologies such as crew safety systems, life-support systems, space medicine, and crew training.
 
• The program is a significant milestone in India’s space exploration journey and aims to position India as a key player in human spaceflight capabilities.

questions.question: Which of the following minerals is found in large quantities in India and holds high economic importance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron ore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Iron ore** is one of the most abundant and economically significant minerals in India, making the country the fourth-largest producer in the world as of 2022.
 
• The majority of iron ore production in India comes from states like Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, and Jharkhand, with Odisha being the largest producer.
 
• India's iron ore is predominantly used in the production of steel, which is critical to the construction, automobile, and infrastructure sectors.
 
• The two main types of iron ore found in India are hematite and magnetite, with hematite being the more dominant type.
 
• India exports significant quantities of iron ore to countries like China and Japan, contributing to its foreign exchange reserves and economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Copper**

 
 
• Copper is an important metal used in electrical equipment, construction, and industrial machinery due to its excellent conductivity and malleability.
 
• India has limited copper reserves, with key mining areas located in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Jharkhand.
 
• India imports a significant amount of its copper requirements to meet domestic demand.
 
 
 
• **Petroleum**
 
 
• Petroleum is a crucial energy resource and raw material for industries like petrochemicals, plastics, and fertilizers.
 
• India is the third-largest consumer of crude oil globally but relies heavily on imports to meet around 85% of its demand.
 
• Major petroleum-producing regions in India include Assam, Gujarat, Rajasthan, and offshore fields in the Mumbai High basin.
 
 
 
• **Tin**
 
 
• Tin is primarily used in soldering, tin plating, and the production of alloys like bronze.
 
• India has very limited tin reserves, with some deposits found in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, making it dependent on imports to meet domestic demand.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

1) Both the Prime Minister (PM) and Chief Minister (CM) can advise dissolution of the respective Lower House.

2) Only the PM can recommend President's Rule under Article 356 of the Constitution.

Which of the statements is/are **correct**?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** Both the **Prime Minister (PM)** and the **Chief Minister (CM)** can advise the dissolution of their respective Lower Houses. **Correct.**

 
 
• The **Prime Minister**, along with the **Council of Ministers**, can advise the **President** to dissolve the **Lok Sabha** under **Article 85** of the Constitution.
 
• Similarly, the **Chief Minister**, along with the **Council of Ministers**, can advise the **Governor** to dissolve the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)** of the state.
 
• The President and Governor generally act on the aid and advice of their respective Councils of Ministers.
 
 ***Hence, Statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 2:** Only the PM can recommend President's Rule under **Article 356** of the Constitution. **Incorrect.**
 
 
• **President's Rule** is imposed by the **President of India** under **Article 356** when a state's constitutional machinery fails.
 
• The recommendation is generally made by the **Union Council of Ministers**, headed by the Prime Minister, and is often based on a report from the **Governor** of the concerned state.
 
• The Constitution does not provide that the **Prime Minister alone** can recommend President's Rule.
 
 ***Hence, Statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Therefore, only Statement 1 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 74** provides that the **President** shall act in accordance with the aid and advice of the **Council of Ministers** headed by the **Prime Minister**.
 
• **Article 163** provides that the **Governor** acts on the aid and advice of the **Council of Ministers** headed by the **Chief Minister**, except in matters where the Constitution grants discretionary powers.
 
• **Article 356** deals with the imposition of **President's Rule** in a state if the constitutional machinery fails.
 
• During **President's Rule**, the powers of the state government are assumed by the **President**, and the state legislature may be suspended or dissolved.
 
• The proclamation of President's Rule must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within **two months** from the date of its issuance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The landmark **S.R. Bommai vs Union of India (1994)** judgment placed significant restrictions on the arbitrary use of **Article 356**.
 
• The **Lok Sabha** is the Lower House at the Union level, while the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)** is the Lower House at the state level.
 
• The power to dissolve the Lower House is exercised formally by the **President** or **Governor**, but usually on the advice of the elected executive.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of type of nutrient - nutrient is correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Micronutrient - Boron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Boron** is classified as a micronutrient because plants require it in very small amounts for proper growth and development.
 
• It plays a critical role in **cell wall formation**, membrane stability, and pollen tube growth in plants.
 
• Deficiency of boron leads to symptoms like **stunted root growth**, hollow stems, or flower abortion in plants.
 
• Boron is absorbed by plants from the soil in the form of **borate ions (BO3³⁻).**
 
• Common sources of boron in agriculture include fertilizers like **borax** and **boric acid**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Micronutrient - Calcium (Option 1):**
 
 
• Calcium is actually a **macronutrient**, not a micronutrient, as it is required by plants in relatively large amounts.
 
• It is essential for cell wall integrity and acts as a secondary messenger in various cellular processes.
 
• Calcium deficiency can lead to problems like **blossom end rot in tomatoes** and weak cell walls in plants.
 
 
 
• **Macronutrient - Zinc (Option 2):**
 
 
• Zinc is a **micronutrient**, not a macronutrient, as it is needed in small quantities by plants.
 
• It is essential for enzyme activation, protein synthesis, and hormone production in plants.
 
• Zinc deficiency often manifests as **chlorosis** (yellowing of leaves) and stunted growth.
 
 
 
• **Macronutrient - Iron (Option 4):**
 
 
• Iron is also a **micronutrient**, not a macronutrient.
 
• It plays a key role in chlorophyll synthesis and acts as a cofactor for various enzymatic reactions.
 
• Iron deficiency is characterized by **interveinal chlorosis** in young leaves.
 
 
 
• **Macronutrients vs Micronutrients:**
 
 
• Macronutrients (e.g., nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium) are required in large amounts by plants, while micronutrients (e.g., zinc, boron, iron) are needed in trace amounts.
 
• Both types of nutrients are vital for plant health, growth, and productivity.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding electromagnetic devices?

options.text: Electric Generator : Converts electrical energy to mechanical energy.
Transformer : Operates on DC current to change voltage.
Electric Bell : Uses the magnetic effect of electric current.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electric Bell: Uses the magnetic effect of electric current.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An electric bell operates on the principle of the **magnetic effect of electric current**, where an electromagnet is created by passing an electric current through a coil of wire.
 
• The magnetic field generated attracts a metal armature, causing it to strike the bell and produce sound.
 
• The electric bell consists of components like an electromagnet, armature, contact screw, and hammer, all working in synchronization to create the ringing sound.
 
• When the circuit is complete, the current flows through the coil, magnetizing the core, and pulling the armature, which simultaneously breaks the circuit and causes the hammer to strike the bell.
 
• This cycle repeats rapidly as long as the switch is pressed, producing a continuous ringing sound.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electric Generator: Converts electrical energy to mechanical energy**

 
 
• This statement is incorrect. An electric generator actually converts **mechanical energy into electrical energy**.
 
• It operates on the principle of electromagnetic induction, as discovered by Michael Faraday, where a conductor moving through a magnetic field induces an electric current.
 
• Generators are widely used in power plants to produce electricity for homes, industries, and businesses.
 
 
 
• **Transformer: Operates on DC current to change voltage**
 
 
• This statement is incorrect because transformers **only work with alternating current (AC)**, not direct current (DC).
 
• Transformers are used to step up (increase) or step down (decrease) the voltage levels in an AC circuit.
 
• They function based on the principle of mutual induction between two coils of wire.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnet: A permanent magnet**
 
 
• This statement is incorrect because an electromagnet is a **temporary magnet** that only exhibits magnetic properties when an electric current flows through its coil.
 
• Once the current is stopped, the magnetic field disappears, unlike a permanent magnet that retains its magnetism.
 
• Electromagnets are widely used in devices like motors, relays, and magnetic cranes.

questions.question:
**Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct options:**

**Assertion (A)**: Mission Amrit Sarovar promotes water conservation.

**Reason (R)**: It aims to construct 75 ponds in each district by 2024.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mission Amrit Sarovar** is a flagship initiative by the Government of India, launched to promote water conservation and sustainable water resource management.
 
• The objective of Mission Amrit Sarovar is to develop and rejuvenate **75 water bodies in every district** across the country by August 15, 2023, as part of the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav celebrations.
 
• The project aims to strengthen water security and ensure environmental sustainability by constructing ponds and water reservoirs to increase water storage and recharge groundwater levels.
 
• The **Reason (R)** correctly explains the **Assertion (A)** since the construction of 75 ponds in each district directly contributes to promoting water conservation efforts.
 
• Mission Amrit Sarovar seeks to involve multiple stakeholders, including rural communities, local bodies, and government agencies, to revive traditional water conservation practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Water Conservation**
 
 
• Water conservation refers to the strategies, policies, and activities aimed at managing the use of fresh water to meet current and future demands sustainably.
 
• It includes measures such as rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge, and the construction of water bodies like ponds and reservoirs.
 
• Programs like Mission Amrit Sarovar align with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG), particularly Goal 6: Clean Water and Sanitation.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Groundwater Recharge**
 
 
• Groundwater recharge is essential for maintaining aquifer levels, which are a critical source of drinking water and irrigation in India.
 
• Constructing ponds and water reservoirs helps in reducing surface runoff and ensures that water infiltrates into the ground, replenishing groundwater levels.
 
 
 
• **Community Participation in Water Conservation**
 
 
• Mission Amrit Sarovar emphasizes the active involvement of local communities in creating and maintaining water bodies.
 
• Such participation fosters awareness about water conservation and ensures the sustainability of the initiative in the long term.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Consider the statements about Rauf:

1. It is a women's group dance of Kashmir usually performed at Eid.

2. Dancers align in two facing rows executing toe-heel footwork called ras. Which is/are **correct**?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3: Both 1 & 2 correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rauf** is a traditional dance form of Kashmir, primarily performed by women during festive occasions such as Eid.
 
• The dance is performed in groups, with women aligning themselves into two facing rows.
 
• Rauf is characterized by intricate toe-heel footwork, which is locally referred to as **ras.**
 
• The dance reflects the vibrant culture and traditions of Kashmir and is a significant representation of its rich heritage.
 
• It is a popular folk dance that also serves as a medium of social interaction and communal harmony among women in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Kashmiri Dances:**

 
 
• Rouf (or Rauf):
 
 
• Who: Performed by women in colorful dresses.
 
• When: Celebrates spring and festivals like Eid and Ramzan.
 
• How: Simple, rhythmic footwork, with dancers facing each other, mimicking bees.
 
 
 
• Dumhal:
 
 
• Who: Exclusively performed by men of the Wattal tribe.
 
• When: Performed on special, auspicious occasions.
 
• How: Dancers wear vibrant robes and conical caps, plant a banner, and dance around it, singing folk songs in chorus.
 
 
 
• Hikat:
 
 
• A simple dance by two girls holding hands, moving clockwise and anti-clockwise, often involving weeding/harvesting themes.
 
 
 
• Bhand Pather:
 
 
• A traditional folk theatre form that combines dance, music, and satire, performed by wandering minstrels (Bhand).

questions.question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the **correct **options:

**Assertion (A)**: India's rank in the Global Happiness Index is lower than most South Asian neighbours.

**Reason (R)**: India's GDP per capita is the lowest in South Asia.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3) A is true, but R is false.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **India's rank in the Global Happiness Index has been consistently low**, with neighboring South Asian countries like Nepal, Bhutan, and Bangladesh often ranking higher.
 
• As per the 2023 World Happiness Report, India ranked **126th out of 137 countries**, while countries like Bhutan ranked significantly higher.
 
• The Global Happiness Index considers factors such as social support, life expectancy, freedom to make life choices, and perceptions of corruption—not just economic indicators like GDP per capita.
 
• India's GDP per capita is **not the lowest in South Asia**. For example, countries like Afghanistan have a lower GDP per capita than India.
 
• Hence, while the assertion (A) is correct that India's rank is lower than most South Asian neighbors, the reason (R) is incorrect since the ranking is based on several factors beyond GDP per capita.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Factors influencing the Global Happiness Index:**

 
 
• The ranking is based on six key metrics: GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom to make life choices, generosity, and perceptions of corruption.
 
• While GDP per capita is an important factor, other social and psychological well-being aspects weigh heavily in the index.
 
• Countries like Bhutan rank higher because of their focus on Gross National Happiness, despite having lower GDP per capita.
 
 
 
• **India's performance in the Global Happiness Index:**
 
 
• India's lower ranking is attributed to factors such as weak social support, perceived corruption, and lower levels of individual freedom.
 
• Efforts to improve quality of life through government initiatives like Digital India, Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, and Ayushman Bharat are aimed at addressing these issues.
 
 
 
• **GDP per capita in South Asia:**
 
 
• India's GDP per capita is higher than several South Asian nations, including Afghanistan and Nepal.
 
• However, countries like Bhutan and Maldives have higher GDP per capita due to their smaller populations and focused economic strategies.

questions.question: Which Indian river was added to the National River Conservation Plan in 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Musi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Musi River, located in Telangana, was added to the National River Conservation Plan (NRCP) in 2024.
 
• The NRCP is an initiative by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) to conserve and rejuvenate polluted rivers across India.
 
• The Musi River flows through Hyderabad and has been heavily polluted due to untreated sewage, industrial waste, and urban runoff.
 
• Under the NRCP, measures such as sewage treatment plants, bio-remediation, riverbank restoration, and public awareness campaigns are implemented to revive polluted rivers.
 
• The inclusion of the Musi River in the NRCP aims to address environmental concerns and improve water quality for better ecological and human health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yamuna River:**

 
 
• The Yamuna River is the largest tributary of the Ganga and flows through several states, including Uttarakhand, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• It has been part of the NRCP since 1993 due to high pollution levels in cities like Delhi and Agra.
 
• Under the NRCP, projects such as sewage treatment, riverfront development, and waste management have been undertaken.
 
 
 
• **Krishna River:**
 
 
• The Krishna River is one of India's major rivers, flowing through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It is known for its importance in irrigation, hydroelectric power generation, and water supply.
 
• The Krishna is not part of the NRCP, as pollution levels are comparatively lower than rivers like the Yamuna or Musi.
 
 
 
• **Gomti River:**
 
 
• The Gomti River flows through Uttar Pradesh, including the city of Lucknow.
 
• It has been part of the NRCP since the late 1990s due to pollution from untreated sewage and industrial effluents.
 
• Efforts under the NRCP include constructing sewage treatment plants and reducing pollution sources.

questions.question: Article 50 is part of which section of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Directive Principles of State Policy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 50 of the Indian Constitution falls under the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, which are outlined in Part IV of the Constitution (Articles 36-51).
 
• It specifically states, "**The State shall take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State**."
 
• The purpose of Article 50 is to maintain the independence of the judiciary, a vital component of a democratic system, and to ensure the impartiality of justice.
 
• DPSPs, including Article 50, are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts, but they act as guiding principles for the State to establish policies and laws.
 
• Article 50 has played a crucial role in the Indian judicial system by emphasizing the doctrine of separation of powers between the judiciary and the executive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• Fundamental Duties are listed under Part IVA of the Indian Constitution (Article 51A).
 
• They were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• These duties serve as moral obligations for citizens to promote a spirit of patriotism and uphold the unity of the nation.
 
• Examples include abiding by the Constitution, respecting the national flag and anthem, protecting the environment, and promoting harmony.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution (Articles 12-35).
 
• They guarantee basic rights to all citizens, essential for their development and protection against state actions.
 
• Key Fundamental Rights include the Right to Equality (Article 14-18), Right to Freedom (Article 19-22), and Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32).
 
• These rights are justiciable, meaning individuals can approach the courts if their rights are violated.
 
 
 
• **Preamble:**
 
 
• The Preamble serves as the introductory statement of the Indian Constitution, outlining its objectives and philosophy.
 
• It declares India as a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, and Democratic Republic and ensures Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity to all its citizens.
 
• Although not enforceable in a court of law, the Preamble is considered a guiding light for interpreting the Constitution.

questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order:

1. GST Council constituted

2. Constitution (101st Amendment) Act enacted

3. GST launched

Choose the correct chronological sequence:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2-1-3**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was implemented in India on **July 1, 2017**, marking the beginning of a unified indirect tax structure across the nation.
 
• Before its launch, the **Constitution (101st Amendment) Act** was enacted on **September 8, 2016**, to provide the legal framework for GST implementation.
 
• The GST Council, which is responsible for making recommendations on GST-related matters, was constituted on **September 15, 2016**.
 
• Hence, the correct chronological order is as follows:
 
 
• **Constitution (101st Amendment) Act enacted (September 8, 2016)**
 
• **GST Council constituted (September 15, 2016)**
 
• **GST launched (July 1, 2017)**
 
 
 
• This sequence aligns with the preparatory steps taken by the Indian government to roll out GST effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016:**

 
 
• The 101st Constitutional Amendment was enacted to introduce GST in India.
 
• It empowered both the Centre and the States to levy and collect GST on goods and services.
 
• The amendment subsumed several indirect taxes such as excise duty, service tax, and VAT into a single tax structure.
 
 
 
• **GST Council:**
 
 
• The GST Council is a constitutional body established under Article 279A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and includes State Finance Ministers as members.
 
• The council is responsible for making recommendations on tax rates, exemptions, and other policy matters related to GST.

questions.question:
Read the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) carefully and choose the **correct **option.

**Assertion (A)**: The IPR 1956 created an industrial classification into Schedules A, B, and C.

**Reason (R)**: This was to identify sectors for exclusive state control, joint sectors, and private sector operation.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) of 1956 was a significant policy document that aimed to classify industries into three categories: Schedule A, Schedule B, and Schedule C.
 
• Schedule A included industries that were exclusively under state control and were regarded as essential for national defense and economic development (e.g., railways, atomic energy).
 
• Schedule B covered industries that were to be developed under joint sector arrangements, i.e., both state and private enterprises could participate in these industries.
 
• Schedule C comprised industries that were to be left for private sector operations, allowing individual entrepreneurship to thrive.
 
• The classification was designed to promote a mixed economy model and was rooted in the philosophy of socialist planning, which sought to balance private and state ownership.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Post-Independence (IPR 1948, 1956): Focused on public sector dominance and planned development.
 
• Liberalization (IPR 1991): Shifted towards opening the economy and global integration.
 
• **Recent Initiatives:**
 
 
• Make in India (2014): To make India a global manufacturing hub.
 
• Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan (2020): Aimed at self-reliance and reducing import dependency.
 
• Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme (2020): Offers incentives for increased domestic production.

questions.question:
Regarding Earth's major climatic zones:

1. Tropical zones experience minimal seasonal temperature variation

2. Temperate zones are characterized by four distinct seasons.

Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3: Both 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1:** Tropical zones experience minimal seasonal temperature variation because they are located near the equator and receive consistent solar radiation throughout the year. This results in relatively stable temperatures.
 
• **Statement 2:** Temperate zones are characterized by four distinct seasons: spring, summer, autumn, and winter. These zones experience significant temperature variations due to their location between the tropical and polar zones.
 
• The Earth's major climatic zones are divided into **tropical, temperate, and polar** zones based on latitude, solar radiation, and prevailing weather patterns.
 
• The tropical zone spans from the Tropic of Cancer to the Tropic of Capricorn and is known for its hot and humid climate, while the temperate zones lie between the tropics and polar regions and experience moderate climates.
 
• The distinction between these zones is important for understanding global weather patterns, biodiversity, and human activities adapted to these climates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Earth's Climatic Zones**

 
 
• The Earth is divided into three major climatic zones based on latitude: tropical, temperate, and polar.
 
• **Tropical Zone:** Located between 23.5°N and 23.5°S, it experiences high temperatures and rainfall year-round.
 
• **Temperate Zone:** Found between 23.5° and 66.5° in both hemispheres, it has distinct seasonal changes and moderate climates.
 
• **Polar Zone:** Situated beyond 66.5° in both hemispheres, it experiences extremely cold temperatures and long winters.
 
• These climatic zones influence global weather patterns, ecosystem diversity, and human adaptation to different environments.
